method: One skill definition executed on two independent physics backends; the recover/fall verdict and the pitch metrics must agree. Both backends share the same torque-limited balance-PD law (KP_BAL/KV_BAL/MAX_TORQUE_BAL from g1_spec.py) and the same inverted-pendulum torso model, so the verdict is engine-independent.

environment.pybullet: stub-only on Windows (real wheel not installable on Windows; dynamic layer CI-gated on Linux)

baseline_runs.note: Measured locally; these are the verdicts the PyBullet CI run must agree with.

static_spec_consistency.note: Both backends generated from one robot spec (g1_spec.py); URDF/joint-chain/link-offsets verified, including the torso_pitch inverted-pendulum hinge.

pybullet_backend_contract.note: PyBullet call surface + failure semantics verified (real PyBullet absent on Windows -> bullet_stub).

dynamic_engine_agreement.note: MuJoCo<->PyBullet numeric agreement runs only where real PyBullet is importable (Linux CI). Skipped on this Windows host; not faked. The PyBullet run must reproduce the three baseline_run verdicts above.
